newsitem.title: USA: Ivax says FDA oks generic drug etodolac.
newsitem.headline: Ivax says FDA oks generic drug etodolac.

text.p: Ivax Corp Monday said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved an Abbreviated New Drug Application for the generic pharmaceutical product etodolac in 400 mg tablets.

Etodolac is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug indicated for use in the management of osteoarthritis and pain, and is the generic equivalent of Wyeth-Ayerst Laboratories' Lodine. Wyeth-Ayerst is the pharmaceutical division of American Home Products Corp. The patent for Lodine expired February 28, 1997.
The product is being marketed by Ivax's wholly-owned subsidiary Zenith Goldline Pharmaceuticals Inc and shipping has commenced.
Ivax is a holding company with subsidiaries engaged primarily in the research, development, manufacture and marketing of health care products.

Separately, Ivax said the FDA granted tentative approval of its Abbreviated New Drug Application for acyclovir in 400 and 800 mg tablets. Acyclovir is indicated for the treatment of genital herpes, herpes zoster (shingles) and chickenpox, and is the generic equivalent of Glaxo Wellcome Plc's Zovirax.
